Each input character at position *i* (0-indexed) in a word of length *n* is shifted by roughly *n − 1 − i* places in the alphabet:

| Pair | Matches len−1−i | Off by +1 |
|---|---|---|
| dog → fpg | d+2=f, o+1=p, g+0=g | — |
| fish → jkth | i+2=k, s+1=t, h+0=h | f+4=j (pos 0) |
| tree → wtff | t+3=w, r+2=t, e+1=f | e+1=f (pos 3) |
| stone → wwqpf | s+4=w, t+3=w, o+2=q | n+2=p (pos 3), e+1=f (pos 4) |

The base rule `shift[i] = n − 1 − i` reproduces 13 of 17 positions exactly.
